sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Pompano Beach?
sections.html:
Pompano Beach sits in northern Broward County, so the property appraiser, tax collector and clerk you deal with are all Broward offices. The city covers over 25 square miles between Miami and Palm Beach, according to the city's own resident page, and its population swells past 150,000 during the winter season when part-time residents return.

That seasonal swing matters when you pick how to sell. A listing in winter meets more buyers on the ground, while a house that needs work or sits empty can wait a long time between showings. The routes below cover the usual choices.

  • List with an agent and accept repairs, showings and a closing date that depends on the buyer's lender.
  • Sell the house yourself and handle pricing, disclosures and paperwork alone.
  • Take a cash offer on the house as it stands, with no repair list and a closing date you pick.

sections.h2: How did Pompano Beach grow, and what does that mean for the houses?
sections.html:
Pompano Beach grew from a small settlement incorporated in 1908, and the word Beach was added on June 16, 1947, when the oceanfront community joined the town. The city's historical pages credit a surveyor with the name, and the fish itself is why the city describes its warm waters as an abundance of pompano.

The housing stock reflects that long, uneven growth. The Census Bureau lists a 2020 population of 112,046 against 99,845 in 2010, and an estimate of 117,211 for July 2025. Older homes near the Intracoastal and the beach sit beside newer condos and townhomes, so condition and age vary a great deal from one block to the next.

The city also points to the 1,000-foot fishing pier, the beachside fishing village and the Hillsboro Inlet lighthouse area as its landmarks. Buyers who want a coastal location pay attention to flood exposure and insurance, so keep your policy, elevation certificate and any roof or window permits ready before you talk price.

sections.h2: How does the Broward homestead exemption affect a Pompano Beach sale?
sections.html:
The exemption stays with the owner and does not pass to the buyer. The Broward County Property Appraiser says the seller's exemptions do not carry past the year of sale, so the buyer must file a fresh application.

Applications run from January 1 through March 1, and Broward lists September 20, 2027 as the last day to late file for the 2027 tax year. The Broward page says rental use would likely forfeit the exemption, so an owner who has been renting the house out should ask the appraiser's office what it means for the final tax bill.

Florida resets a property to just value on January 1 after a change of ownership, which is why the tax bill a buyer pays can sit well above the seller's. The Florida Department of Revenue explains that a sale, foreclosure or transfer of title triggers the reset, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses. If you want a quick check on what a buyer may face, ask the Broward appraiser's office.

  • Keep your exemption receipt, which Broward mails in early January.
  • Tell the appraiser when you no longer live in the house.
  • Ask about portability if you are buying another Florida home, since the savings can follow you within three years.

sections.h2: What changed in 2026 for Florida property taxes?
sections.html:
Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, and it takes effect January 1, 2027. The Volusia County Property Appraiser describes it as raising the homestead exemption for non-school taxes to up to $150,000 in 2027 and up to $250,000 in 2028, and as cutting the non-homestead assessment cap from 10 percent to 5 percent.

The same office says implementing legislation still has to settle some details, so the effect on a given Pompano Beach house is not fixed. For a seller, the change speaks to timing: a buyer who plans to live in the house may weigh future homestead savings, while an investor buying a non-homestead property faces a different cap. Ask the Broward County Property Appraiser how the new rules apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: What closing costs and transfer steps apply in Pompano Beach?
sections.html:
Florida charges documentary stamp tax on a deed at 70 cents per $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, according to the Department of Revenue. The department adds that all parties to the document are liable, so who pays is a matter for the contract.

The clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded. Recording charges under section 28.24 start at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each further page, with extra per-page fees on top, so ask the Broward clerk for a current total.

  • Order a payoff letter from each lender so liens are cleared at closing.
  • Pull the Broward tax bill and ask the title company to prorate it.
  • Check for open permits and code violations with the city's building office before you sign.
  • Confirm who signs the deed and that two witnesses are lined up, as Florida requires.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Pompano Beach house with tenants, liens or an inherited title?
sections.html:
Yes, though each case adds steps. A rented house can sell with the tenant in place, and Florida lets a landlord end a month-to-month tenancy with at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period under section 83.57. Nonpayment starts with a written three-day notice under section 83.56.

With a tax lien or a foreclosure, the clock matters. In a judicial foreclosure the clerk sells the property between 20 and 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to more time, and the winning bidder posts a 5 percent deposit. Selling before that date can protect your equity.

For an inherited house, Florida allows summary administration when the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000, or when the decedent has been dead more than two years. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxable for documentary stamps, according to the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Is a cash sale faster than listing in Pompano Beach?
faqs.a: It can be, because a cash buyer does not wait on a lender appraisal. The seller still needs a clear title, a payoff for each lien and a recorded deed with two witnesses.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamps on a Pompano Beach deed?
faqs.a: The contract decides, but the Department of Revenue says all parties to the document are liable for the tax. The rate outside Miami-Dade is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Broward says the seller's exemptions do not carry past the year of sale, and the buyer files a new application by March 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I am behind on the mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sale closes before the foreclosure sale date. After final judgment the clerk sets the sale between 20 and 35 days out unless the plaintiff agrees to later, so move early.

faqs.q: Where do I get a recorded copy of my deed?
faqs.a: Ask the Broward County clerk's records division, which records deeds and collects the stamp tax at recording. Bring the instrument and the recording fee.
